preview: **Verdict: No usable edge from the disclosure date after costs for a long-only swing desk on our 20 tickers. No signals.json changes.**
## 1. Evidence

- **Pre-STOCK Act, positive but measured from the trade date:** Senate purchases beat the market by 85 bp/month from 1993 to 1998 ([Ziobrowski, JFQA 2004](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journ
- **Rebuttal:** actual portfolios lagged the market by 2 to 3% a year from 2004 to 2008 ([Eggers & Hainmueller, JOP 2013](https://andy.egge.rs/papers/EggMueller_capitol_losses_jop_2013.pdf)).

note.text:
RESEARCH INC. ANALYST NOTE (2026-10-14)
Hot September CPI (3.7% YoY, core 2.6%, both above forecast) put an Oct 28 Fed hike back on the table and gave the S&P 500 (-1.1%) and Nasdaq (-1.9%) their worst day since July; the Dow held near flat.
The damage was in AI and chips: semis (SOXX) fell 4.5%, AMD 5.7%, NVDA 3.2%, LITE 9.3%. Small caps (IWM) lost 1.9%. Money hid in health care (+2.5%) and staples (+2.2%).
Our ideas were mixed: UNH +4.7% and BLK +0.7% worked, but ASML gave back 3.9% with the chip selloff. LITE and AMT/CCI swings from last week are now under water or flat.
Avoids did their job: BAC fell 4.8% on its $1.2B money-laundering settlement, and airlines dropped 3.6% to 4.1% with Brent still above $105.
Next: PPI Thursday 8:30 AM is the next inflation test, then NFLX (Oct 20) and TSLA (Oct 21) earnings. Hold off on new chip and high-beta entries until yields settle.
